title: disktree: see what fills your disk, then free it
notes: Facts from github.com/tobi/disktree (README, 2026-10-04). `text` is shown and aligned; `say` is read.

lines.text: Shopify founder Tobi Lütke just shipped a disk cleaner.
say: Shopify founder Toby Lootkee just shipped a disk cleaner.

lines.text: Run it as administrator on Windows, and it reads a four-million-file drive in about three point four seconds.
say: Run it as administrator on Windows, and it reads a four million file drive in about three point four seconds.

lines.text: In his test, WizTree took eleven.
say: In his test, Wiz Tree took eleven.

lines.text: It's called disktree. It's free, open source, and runs on Linux, Mac and Windows.
say: It's called disk tree.
It's free, open source, and runs on Linux, Mac and Windows.

lines.text: The idea is simple. Every folder becomes a box, sized by what it really costs on disk, with boxes inside boxes all the way down.
say: The idea is simple.
Every folder becomes a box, sized by what it really costs on disk, with boxes inside boxes all the way down.

lines.text: Scroll, and you zoom into a folder until it fills the screen, then drop straight inside.
say: Scroll, and you zoom into a folder until it fills the screen, then drop straight inside.

lines.text: Color tells you what kind of data it is: code, toolchains, media, documents, caches.
say: Color tells you what kind of data it is: code, toolchains, media, documents, caches.

lines.text: And diagonal stripes mark space you can get back, like caches and build output.
say: And diagonal stripes mark space you can get back, like caches and build output.

lines.text: It even counts hidden folders, because a hidden cache is often the biggest thing in your home folder.
say: It even counts hidden folders, because a hidden cache is often the biggest thing in your home folder.

lines.text: Found the culprit? Mark it, and it takes the danger color, along with everything inside it.
say: Found the culprit?
Mark it, and it takes the danger color, along with everything inside it.

lines.text: Nothing is deleted yet. You review the list first.
say: Nothing is deleted yet.
You review the list first.

lines.text: Then pick the trash, which you can undo, or delete permanently, which always asks first.
say: Then pick the trash, which you can undo, or delete permanently, which always asks first.

lines.text: When it's done, it scans again and shows how much space you really got back.
say: When it's done, it scans again and shows how much space you really got back.

lines.text: One key even copies the list as a prompt for your coding agent, to check each path before removing it.
say: One key even copies the list as a prompt for your coding agent, to check each path before removing it.

lines.text: The catch? It guesses what a folder is from its name, so some colors can be wrong on your machine.
say: The catch?
It guesses what a folder is from its name, so some colors can be wrong on your machine.

lines.text: Still, seeing exactly where your space went, before deleting anything, is worth a lot.
say: Still, seeing exactly where your space went, before deleting anything, is worth a lot.

lines.text: That's today's tool. There's a new one every day.
